sources.text: A new office should sit closest to the doors we still need: the untouched doors in our turf, weighted by how many doors each precinct has left. Untouched or lightly touched precincts (under 25 percent of doors touched) that are dense (over 2,000 doors per square mile) are worth a new office; sparse precincts (under 1,000 doors per square mile) are slow to knock and are better handled at the end with drive-out shifts. Candidate sites are listed in the candidate office sites table.

Every Monday we send the client one table for the week that ended Sunday, one row per office plus a total: doors, contacts, registration cards, and paid hours. Doors and contacts use our dashboard definitions (doors once per day, rollbacks removed). Cards are valid registration cards, duplicates removed. Hours are paid hours for GOTV and registration shifts together; shifts still missing a clock out are left out and noted.
